ai.title: Increase request timeout to 20s and update error message
ai.summary: The `requestTimeout` in `npm-app/release/index.js` increased from 10000 to 20000 ms. The timeout rejection in `httpGet` now includes 'Please check your internet connection and try again.' to clarify network issues.

eli5.text: If a network request to download a release takes too long, it now waits up to 20 seconds before giving up instead of 10. When that timeout happens, the error message now clearly says 'Please check your internet connection and try again.' instead of just 'Request timeout'. This affects anyone using the release tooling that downloads assets over a network. The change is live today in the main release script.

ai.title: Simplify timeout error in release script
ai.summary: The `httpGet` function in `npm-app/release/index.js` now rejects with a concise 'Request timeout.' message instead of a verbose connection-check instruction. This detailed guidance moved to the `ensureBinaryExists` catch block, ensuring users receive specific troubleshooting advice only when binary download failures occur.

eli5.text: If you try to download the tool behind the scenes and it takes too long, you will now just see the short message 'Request timeout.' rather than a long sentence telling you to check your internet connection. That longer hint now only appears if the main download step actually fails, so the basic timeout keeps its simple wording. This is a small behind-the-scenes tweak to the release helper, already live today, and it only changes what message you see during a long download.

ai.title: PTY fallback to child process on native load failure
ai.summary: Wraps `require('bun-pty')` in try/catch within `npm-app/src/native/pty.ts`, exporting `bunPty` as `undefined` on failure and logging platform/arch/BUN_PTY_LIB. `npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts` gates PTY usage on `bunPty` truthiness, falling back to `runBackgroundCommand` child process. `IPty` type updated to `ReturnType<NonNullable<typeof bunPty>['spawn']>` to reflect optional native binding.

eli5.text: If the app's terminal helper that normally runs your shell commands fails to load on your computer, it now quietly skips that helper and runs commands through a basic built-in method instead, so your terminal still works. The developers only turn on this fallback when the primary helper is missing or broken, and they made it log which computer type was affected so they can investigate. You'd notice nothing different unless the helper is unavailable, in which case the terminal keeps working instead of stopping.

ai.title: Replace term.writeLine with console.log in release rate-limit fallback
ai.summary: Swapped `term.writeLine` for `console.log` in the GitHub API rate-limit fallback path within `npm-app/release/index.js`. This ensures the warning message outputs correctly regardless of terminal library initialization state or TTY availability. Scope limited to the internal release tooling script.

eli5.text: When the release team's tool checks for new versions using GitHub's API and hits the rate limit, it now shows the warning message reliably on screen. Previously, the message might have failed to appear because it depended on a special terminal setup that wasn't always ready. This is a behind-the-scenes fix for the internal release tooling, so only the engineers who run the release process would notice the difference. The change is live today.

ai.title: Fix npm-app types
ai.summary: Removed `paths` alias `@/*` from `npm-app/tsconfig.json` and replaced import `@/utils/logger` with relative path `../utils/logger` in `npm-app/src/native/pty.ts`. This resolves type resolution issues for the npm-app package.

eli5.text: The internal tool that powers the npm-app package had a wiring problem where a helper module was being referenced by a nickname that only worked in certain folders. Developers running or building the package were seeing type errors and failures because that nickname wasn't being recognized. The tool was fixed so it now points directly to the helper file using its real location, and the nickname system was turned off for this package. You wouldn't notice this directly, but if you're building or running this package, your commands and error logs will now be cleaner and succeed where they previously failed.

ai.title: Release check uses Atom feed
ai.summary: getLatestVersion in npm-app/release/index.js now fetches GitHub releases.atom instead of api.github.com. XML regex extracts tag from <id> node. Eliminates 403 rate-limit fallback logic. Internal release tooling only.

eli5.text: The program that checks for new versions of this software before release used to ask GitHub's main API for the latest version, which often blocked the check when too many people asked in the same hour. It now reads a simpler, public feed of releases instead, so the version check no longer fails when GitHub throttles requests. Only the internal team that publishes releases is affected; you won't see any difference unless you run that publishing step yourself.

ai.title: Refactor rage detection to use object-based key events with filtering
ai.summary: CLI key handling now passes raw `{ str, key }` objects to `keyMashingDetector.recordEvent` instead of pre-filtering strings. `createCountDetector` accepts an optional `filter` callback to determine event inclusion, replacing hardcoded modifier/special-key checks in `rage-detectors.ts`. Object comparison in repeat detection uses `JSON.stringify` to correctly group identical key events. This internal refactor centralizes filtering logic within the detector configuration.

eli5.text: If you repeatedly mash random keys in the terminal, the app will now catch that pattern. It now passes each key press, along with its modifier and name, as a single unit to the rage detector, which then decides what to count via a configurable rule instead of a fixed one. Identical key presses are grouped correctly, and ctrl+C is still counted as a rage trigger. Because this lives entirely in the app's internal wiring, you won't see anything new on screen.

ai.title: Release script prints latest GitHub Actions run URL
ai.summary: The release script now fetches the latest workflow run ID before and after triggering the release-binaries.yml workflow to print a direct link to the new run. This replaces the static monitor URL with a dynamic link to the specific action run, falling back to the general actions page if the ID cannot be determined. The change is isolated to npm-app/scripts/release.js.

eli5.text: When you trigger a software release from the internal tooling, the assistant now waits a moment and then prints a direct link to the specific release progress page, instead of only pointing to the general releases overview. This only affects people running releases through the npm-app scripts folder, and it's live today. If you trigger a release, you'll see a new line with the exact progress URL; if that link can't be found, it falls back to the general releases page.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.336
ai.summary: Version in npm-app/release/package.json bumped from 1.0.335 to 1.0.336. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: The assistant's release process just quietly moved to a new version label, so new copies you download are stamped with the latest number instead of the previous one. While you're updating, this release also lengthens how long the assistant waits for a response before giving up, makes the error message clearer when it does time out, and improves a few behind-the-scenes checks that keep the release flowing smoothly. You won't see new features or speed changes from this update, just a more patient and informative assistant under the hood.

ai.title: Add preuninstall script to delete binary
ai.summary: Added preuninstall script to npm-app/release/package.json to remove the codebuff binary from ~/.config/manicode/ during package uninstallation. This ensures clean removal of platform-specific executables (codebuff or codebuff.exe) when users run npm uninstall. The change is internal to the packaging metadata and does not affect runtime behavior.

eli5.text: When you uninstall CodeBuff, the program will now automatically delete its main executable file from your computer's config folder (located at ~/.config/manicode/ on Linux/Mac or %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\manicode\ on Windows). Previously, running uninstall would leave this binary file behind, potentially taking up space or causing confusion. The cleanup now happens as part of the standard uninstall process - you don't need to do anything extra or manually remove files. This change affects anyone using CodeBuff through the npm-app release package and is live today.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.337
ai.summary: Release package version updated to 1.0.337 in `npm-app/release/package.json`. Internal version increment for `codebuff` package.

eli5.text: The assistant software was updated to a newer version number, which rolls up several smaller improvements users will actually experience. When someone uninstalls the program, it now cleans up an extra leftover file automatically. Network requests that were waiting too long will time out sooner at 20 seconds and show a clearer error message instead of hanging. If the main terminal screen fails to load, the program can fall back to a simpler backup method so it keeps working. Rate-limit notices in the release flow now go to the console instead of an extra screen line, and type-related issues in the npm app have been corrected. These changes are live today for anyone who updates to the new version.

ai.title: Robust binary version check and cleanup in release script
ai.summary: npm-app/release/index.js replaces synchronous execSync with asynchronous spawn for getCurrentVersion, adding timeout handling and error resolution. downloadBinary now deletes existing binary files before fetching new versions to prevent corruption. checkForUpdates triggers downloads when version checks return 'error' or when versions mismatch.

eli5.text: When the software starts up, it now asks the helper program what version is installed, and if that question times out or fails, it quietly treats it like the version is out of date instead of crashing. Before downloading an updated helper, it first deletes any copy left over from a previous attempt, so a half-finished file from a crash or power loss can't corrupt the new one. This only affects the part of the program that manages its own updates, and it is already live.

ai.title: Revert untested release workflow link printing
ai.summary: Reverts the attempt to print the specific GitHub Actions run URL in `npm-app/scripts/release.js`. The logic fetching pre/post workflow run IDs to construct the link is removed due to being untested. The script now logs a generic monitor URL after triggering the workflow.

eli5.text: When a new software release is started, the system used to try to find and print a direct link to watch that specific release process in progress, but that feature was unreliable because it had never been tested. The code that looked up the release details has been removed, and now the system simply tells you to go a single fixed page where you can watch all releases happen. This is a behind-the-scenes stability fix that makes the release-starting process simpler and less likely to mislead you with a broken link.

ai.title: Remove verbose debug logs from auth and websocket middleware
ai.summary: Commented out debug log statements in `backend/src/util/check-auth.ts` and `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts`. This reduces noise from successful authentication and organization repository coverage checks. Internal change only; no user-facing impact.

eli5.text: The system stopped writing success messages to its internal logs when sign-ins and organization repository checks work normally; those checks still happen, but the background tool no longer records a note each time. This only affects the behind-the-scenes diagnostic logs that developers use to investigate problems, so there is nothing you would see or do differently. The change is already live today and applies only to internal logging.

ai.title: Add bun run inf to db:studio script
ai.summary: Updated `db:studio` script in `common/package.json` to prepend `bun run inf` to the `drizzle-kit studio` command. This aligns the script with other database commands (`db:generate`, `db:migrate`) which already use `bun run inf` for environment/infrastructure handling. Scope limited to `common/package.json`.

eli5.text: When you open the database browser tool to explore your data in a visual editor, it now properly loads your environment settings (like credentials and connection details) the same way the other database tools do. Previously, the browser tool skipped this setup step, which could cause it to fail to connect. This change makes all the database commands work through a consistent setup path, so the visual editor will now open reliably alongside the schema generation and migration commands.
